subject: PrivDep: Data transfer matrix, subprocessor map & keystore safeguarding for Eurasia rollout
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@medicahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jun 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private deploy questions — where keys live and what subprocessors touch EU data

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving fast on the private deployment evaluation; legal asked for two concrete things before we proceed to procurement: a current subprocessor map scoped to private deployments (which subprocessors will operate on our VPC/on‑prem control plane) and a clear statement of how customer‑managed keys are used, including any escrow/escrow‑access process you support for on‑prem scenarios.

Specific asks from our side:
- A CSV that lists subprocessors, region of operation, and roles (monitoring, backup, operator, telemetry).
- Whether Redwood ever receives unencrypted model context for requests originating in a customer VPC if customer managed keys are used.
- If break‑glass is available, what triggers and audit steps exist (operator access windows, approvals, log exports).

Can you put together what you can share and mark anything that must be redacted for IP/security reasons? Attaching our vendor questionnaire too.

Cheers,
Sam
Director of Platform Security
Medica Health

Attachment: medica_vendor_q_2025.pdf (pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 14:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — where keys live and what subprocessors touch EU data

Sam —

Appreciate the clear asks. I'm looping in Karthik (Legal/Product) and Soojin (Infra/Private Deploy) to assemble the subprocessor map and keystore/escrow notes. Quick answers up front:

- We'll provide a subprocessor CSV scoped to Private (VPC/on‑prem) showing roles and region of operation; items marked "sensitive" will be redacted with an explanation.
- For Private deployments that opt for customer‑managed keys (bring‑your‑own‑KMS or customer keystore), Redwood's control plane does not hold plaintext customer inputs or derived context at rest. Runtime KVs used by the model are encrypted under customer keys; operator access to decrypted tokens requires an explicit break‑glass workflow.
- Break‑glass: yes — time‑bounded, approval‑logged, with tamper‑evident audit exports. We'll attach the draft protocol.

We'll send the CSV + keystore_escrow_protocol_draft by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Rachel
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:31:00 +0000
Subject: RE: PrivDep subprocessor map & keystore handling — legal notes

Team —

I've reviewed Sam's vendor questionnaire. A few legal clarifications we should capture in the draft: 

1) Subprocessor visibility: provide an explicit table of subprocessors by role and whether they have any cryptographic key material access. For ones that do, add a short justification and whether they are bound by a DPA addendum.

2) Data egress guarantees: for VPC private deployments we should commit to "no egress of plaintext customer content to Redwood systems" except under break‑glass. For on‑prem packaged installs, same plus a statement that updates/patches are delivered as signed packages; remote support only runs with customer approval.

3) Escrow: we can offer a keystore escrow option for customers that require vendor-assisted key recovery. This should be an opt‑in addendum with signed retrieval procedures, dual custody, and notarized access logs. Add a statement that escrow retrieval requires two independent approvals and an audit export to the customer.

4) Cross‑border transfer: where subprocessors are in non‑EEA jurisdictions we must call out any transfer mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, or customer consent). Don't promise more than we can prove.

Please validate the attached keystore_escrow_protocol_draft for accuracy — Soojin, can you confirm the operational steps and logging behavior?

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: PrivDep subprocessor map & keystore handling — operational confirmation

Karthik / Rachel —

Confirmed on the operational side. Summary of how it works today for Private (VPC/on‑prem):

- Customer keys: supported via two modes — (A) Bring‑Your‑Own‑KMS (customer gives us a keystore endpoint in their VPC) or (B) Customer keystore appliance (on‑prem) with an HSM. In both modes we never persist unencrypted symmetric keys in Redwood control plane. Runtime artifacts (model KV/attention caches) are encrypted (envelope encryption) under the customer key.

- Operator access: break‑glass is a GRANT issued via the customer's identity provider with a signed approval token. Requests to unlock are logged locally and a copy of the approval token and audit log is pushed to the customer's audit bucket (S3/GCS) while we maintain a tamper‑evident record for our internal compliance team.

- Subprocessors: monitoring and telemetry agents (for Dedicated host health) may be operated by third parties in certain regions. Those agents only receive anonymized telemetry by default; any operator troubleshooting that requires request context must be performed via the break‑glass flow and is time‑limited.

- Cross‑border: where a third party operator lives outside the EEA we use SCCs + Data Processing Addendum. For customers requiring EU‑only processing we can offer region‑restricted pools and an audit commitment.

I'll attach an exportable CSV (eu-data-transfer-matrix.csv) and the subproc map (privdep_subproc_map_v1.xlsx). I recommend redacting vendor contact emails in the public copy and sharing a full copy under an NDA if Medica's procurement asks.

Soojin
Director, Private Deploy Operations

Attachment: privdep_subproc_map_v1.xlsx (xlsx); keystore_escrow_protocol_draft.pdf (pdf); eu-data-transfer-matrix.csv (csv)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — package + next steps

Sam / Ivan —

Thanks — attached is the Private‑scope package we discussed: the subprocessor map, EU transfer matrix, and the keystore escrow protocol draft. High level commitments: 

- For Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments with customer‑managed keys, Redwood will not access plaintext customer request content except under a documented and auditable break‑glass event.
- Break‑glass requires two independent approvals (customer approver + Redwood Ops approver), an expiry window, and an automated export of decrypted session logs to a customer audit bucket.
- Subprocessors in the EU/EEA will be used for monitoring/ops; non‑EEA subprocessors will be covered by SCCs and called out in the CSV.

Next actions:
1) Sam — confirm whether you want the redacted public CSV or a full copy under NDA.
2) Ivan — if Medica requires EU‑only processing pools, we can scope a Dedicated capacity in eu‑west with region restriction; I'll follow up with a pricing note.
3) Karthik — can we prepare the DPA addendum passages for keystore escrow and break‑glass so procurement has language to redline?

If helpful we can set a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the protocol.

Cheers,
Rachel
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
